Mathematical equations governing the model's development during mechanical testing are then derived and solved using a particular numerical method. In particular, a novel coupling of the Chen-Marcus crystallization model and the thermomechanical model is implemented and applied to describe the stress-strain behavior and microstructural evolution of strain-induced crystallizing polymers. A notable finding is that previously observed stress anomalies in synthetic data can be attributed to existing folded chains contributing to elasticity and facilitating local chain realignment. A unique numerical challenge is overcome, allowing for an efficient and accurate solution to be obtained.

To better fully describe the paramagnetic response to external magnetic fields applied perpendicular to the superconductor's symmetry axis, a revised Ginzburg-Landau theory is presented. This presentation includes a specific response component arising from the nematic character. Through applying the corresponding equations, the paramagnetic response is calculated, showing a shift from the GL theory's initial prediction by a factor of 1/3. This adjustment is interpretible as the magnetic response of magnetic moments located on orbital planes of individual electrons within triplet Cooper pairs.

A widely used digital communication detection method, differential continuous phase modulation (CPM), is prone to a specific type of timing error known as delay enhancement. This issue results in an unnecessary reduction of the data signal and an increased susceptibility to interference, largely due to the interaction between adjacent data symbols. This paper presents a straightforward method to counter the negative effects of delay misdetction, by accurately identifying the error and calculating the time shift, it is possible to correct the issue at the detector with minimal impact on the device. A simulation study shows that this detection method can significantly minimize timing error and improve performance, even in comparison to other existing solutions.

We introduce the concept of quantum competence in spacetime, linked to the compressibility of its vacuum. This property varies with temperature, allowing us to divide space into three quantum temperature zones based on a characteristic temperature $T_q$. At low temperatures ($T \ll T_q$, Zone 1), the vacuum exhibits incompressibility, leading to the quantization of electromagnetic fields and the integrity of special relativity. As temperatures approach and exceed $T_q$ (Zone 2, $T \approx T_q$), vacuum becomes compressible, possibly causing failures in special relativity and signal interference due to virtual particle deactivation. A Planckian temperature regime (Zone 3, $T \gtrsim T_{\rm Pl}$) experiences extensive deactivation of virtual particles, essential for understanding black hole thermodynamics and quantum gravity. These concepts are further explored using a compressible vacuum Spacetime Algebra and may have significant cosmological and astrophysical implications.

We present ATOMIC, an innovative reasoner that embodies the concept of "machine common knowledge" as posited by cognitive scientists and logicians. By incorporating pre-encoded simple rules about the world, ATOMIC engages in complex inference tasks that require understanding of causality, quantity, and contradiction. Our approach utilizes a chain-of-thought reasoning framework and integrates these rationality priors into the reasoning process. To validate our reasoner's efficacy, we developed a dataset spanning 1,654 intricate mathematical and scientific problems, comparing our method against existing models through extensive experiments. The results highlight the significance of machine common knowledge in enhancing reasoning capabilities, with ATOMIC demonstrating a 26.5% success rate in solving novel, randomised counterfactual problems.

Precious近期限期量子设备，旨在通过开发有价值的量子软件应用来展现其潜力。然而，开发真正有影响力的量子软件应用面临着一个巨大的挑战，由于嘈杂的量子硬件表现不佳，许多现成经典应用已经表现出优越的性能。本研究致力于解决这一难题，通过探索有影响力的混合量子经典软件应用的组合，通过对比单一量子或经典组件，展示了在多个评估维度上的优越性。我们在多个任务场景中验证了所提出的量子软件应用的优势，包括高频交易中的量化投资组合管理，通过整合 HHL 算法构建的回归模型。通过对 HHL 算法在嘈杂环境中的适用性进行深入的可行性分析，我们为近期限期量子设备的软件开发计划提供了宝贵的指引。

In processing language and speech data, attention mechanisms have significantly
improved the performance of neural machines.  However, their efficacy when
combining multiple modalities of learning is yet to be fully explored.  We
introduce a novel multi-modal training approach, BIFA, which employs a
bi-directional informed focus to sequence speech.  This innovative method
leverages two distinct but related attention mechanisms that exploit mutual
knowledge.  We apply BIFA to a joint speech-text recognition task as a
practical use case.  Our results show that incorporating BIFA yields
better results than other attention-based multi-modal methods, achieving a 3.63
points reduction in word error rate (WER) with audio2text data and 0.83 points
with text2audio data on the LJSpeech corpus.  Our code is publicly accessible
at: https://github.com/yuxuanwang/AudioTextSpeechOrientationModel.  BIFA model
demonstrates the value of using speech and text to sequence speech, as well as
the effectiveness of the informed focus mechanism in this context.

This paper investigates the limiting positions of cars in a random uniform parking distribution of n cars across the integer line. We find that, theoretically, the positions of cars for small values of n follow the same distribution as a known process called the discrete self-avoiding walk, both of which have limit processes that can be modeled using systems of interacting particles. However, a key difference arises, where the limit system for parking functions is derived from a specific equation, while the process for self-avoiding walk differs significantly. We provide a statistical analysis to highlight this distinction. Furthermore, we examine the behavior of the first car's position in self-avoiding walk and parking functions, finding that, on average, this position moves to the right at a rate of approximately 0.78 units for every increase of n. We also find that the distribution of self-avoiding walk's limit system differs from its continuous counterpart by a factor of 1.35.

Non-equilibrium quantum phase slips were predicted to be a critical quantum phenomenon that limits DC conductivity in superconducting nanowires. It was also proposed that measuring this effect is highly impractical due to the difficulty of isolating phase slip dynamics from decoherence and damping. Contrary to this belief, we found that gate-tunable measurements on NbN nanowires clearly exhibit non-equilibrium phase slip behavior, characterized by a distinct combination of power-law and saturation regions. Notably, we observed that phase slip dynamics result in non-linear DC conductivity that increases with bias voltage at a particular rate, miraring earlier experiments and theoretical expectations for non-equilibrium phase slip physics.

Accurate video forecasting is crucial for autonomous vehicles to safely navigate and make decisions. This research proposes an innovative framework for generating future video frames that accounts for varying vehicle viewpoints. Unlike existing methods, our approach does not require extensive scene data, relying instead on easily accessible data such as vehicle views. A dual representation is created, linking varying vehicle viewpoints to invariant background elements, which is then used to predict future video frames. By focusing on accessible vehicle viewpoint data, our model generates a more complex and varied model than traditional approaches, which can be seen as a form of unsupervised learning. To achieve this, we employ a novel graph-based method that has three key components: a joint embedding space, an attention mechanism, and a generative flow-based model. Our proposed solution is assessed through various video forecasting tasks and demonstrates significant improvements over current techniques.

This study provides an inter-orbital interaction proof without relying on theoretical inter-orbital competition, which is commonly cited, or theoretical-integrable models, which are also frequently cited. Inter-orbital competition or the inclusion of inter-orbital integrals is p-wave-specific, yet our findings occur in s-wave systems. By utilizing UV-laser-assisted Kapitza-Dirac cooling and cooling with optical molasses, our experiment achieved an enhanced matter-wave interference pattern by two perpendicular atomic orbitals. This enabled an inter-orbital interaction demonstration through our experiment.

The Ω-baryon, first predicted by Gell-Mann and Okun, has a rich history of theoretical significance but a troubled history of detection.
First observed in cosmic rays in 1959, it was disputed as real until the Brookhaven NA49 collaboration confirmed its authenticity in 2000.
With upcoming heavy ion collision experiments at the FAIR and NICA accelerators, there's a need for a refined analysis of multi-strange matter production.
However, current production forecasts rely on inaccurate Ω-baryon resonance cross sections and missing branching ratio data.
This paper aims to fill that gap by comprehensively utilizing the quark model to predict the Ω-baryon resonance spectrum, determining their decay patterns into Kaon and anti-Ket particles, ultimately providing an expanded list of relevant reactions for future research.

Current air contamination models for indoor environments, such as those affecting air quality on urban buses, are generally simplified. These models rely on assumptions that are considered outdated and inaccurate in light of recent advances in research. One such assumption involves using the well-mixed framework to model air contamination, which posits that contaminants are evenly distributed within an enclosed space. While widely adopted due to its ease of use and availability of data requirements, high-level simulations like computational fluid dynamics position schemes are now feasible, provided accurate measurements of relevant parameters are obtainable. To assess the benefits of using a more precise modeling approach over the well-mixed framework, a set of simulations were conducted and validated against real-world data collected from an urban bus. They showed that recent schemes provide significant improvements in simulation accuracy over the well-mixed framework, although its applicability may be restricted in certain scenarios as a result of its data requirements.

We employed first-principle calculations to investigate the spin-orbit effects arising from Cobalt layers adjacent to Bismuth interfaces, and the resulting modifications in the Spin Hall and Anomalous Hall conductivities were found to be significant.  By the modification of carrier populations near the Fermi level, localized states emerge that may scatter off the interface, altering the Spin Hall conductivities. Our analysis indicates that this effect may lead to an increase in Spin Hall angles suitable for Spin-orbit-tunabled devices. We further suggest that this model can be applied to other heavy metal/ferrimagnetic multilayers to identify optimal compositions for such applications.

This paper solves the time-independent fractional Schrödinger equation in multiple dimensions for a generalized Mie-like potential, which includes the Mie potential as a special case. By applying a Jumarie type fractional derivative to a fractional differential model, we obtain solutions for the M-dimensional (where M is greater than or equal to 2) system. Additionally, we obtain the solutions for the M=1 system by applying a suitable transformation to the solutions obtained for the M>=2 system. The solutions are obtained using a fractional differential transformation method and yield accurate results with reduced computational efforts. We also obtain the non-fractional results as special cases and obtain the connection between the generalized and Mie-like hyperradial functions. By applying a fractional differential transformation method to the fractional differential model, we obtain solutions for the generalized Mie-like potential, which yields the Mie-like potential as a special case, which in turn yields the Mie quantum dot as another special case. By comparing our solutions obtained using the fractional differential transformation method with solutions obtained using other methods, we confirm the reliability and efficiency of our approach.

We analyzed whether enforcing a libcartographic consistency threshold of one unit helps a neural network to generalize effectively. We found that this method provides implicit regularization, similar to other network regularization methods, but unlike them, it does not require the training data. This method also leads to a network that is capable of generalizing even when given inputs that are significantly different from the training data. This distinct feature sets it apart from other methods, as they often produce comparable results to traditional training methods, but our method produces notably better outcomes. Moreover, this advantage is particularly pronounced in scenarios where noise levels are high. This method also leads to the derivation of a new norm that is comparable to other previously derived norms, but it leads to a network that is much more robust to inconsistent data, it yields a network with a lower risk of overfitting.

We investigated the Drell-Yan production of colorless leptoquark pairs in third-generation gauge vector leptoquark models, which require at least two gluon interactions. Since this process is suppressed by a high power of the strong coupling constant, it could potentially provide a way to test these models at the Large Hadron Collider. By presenting the leading-order cross sections for various leptoquark masses and comparing them to experimental data from the Large Hadron Collider, we found that the predicted number of events might be within reach of the Large Hadron Collider for top quark leptoquarks with a wide range of masses in a 120 TeV scenario. For charm quark leptoquark leptoquarks, they may be observable for very high luminosity runs at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider with a $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV center-of-mass energy. A dedicated analysis for signed muon final states was also presented.

Radiation exposure during positron emission tomography (PET) scans is minimized by lowering the number of detected photons, but this is often associated with a decline in the clarity of the resulting images. To address this limitation, a neural network was trained to generate high-quality PET images from low-quality ones and corresponding T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging data. A novel uncertainty estimation neural network was developed to minimize expected variance among multiple possible results, enabling the selection of the most reliable PET image output. This uncertainty estimation network is particularly useful for identifying and managing data points that fall outside the expected distribution. By estimating the probability of each pixel's assessed risk, the network can provide a more accurate assessment of polysemantic points, which is in turn employed to filter out outliers. Experimental results show that this method outperforms existing techniques in terms of image fidelity and structural similarity, particularly when dealing with points outside the expected distribution, as long as they are common within the corresponding magnetic resonance imaging images.

A linguistic analysis technique known as Centering Theory (CT) posits that coreference within a text segment is determined by discourse context rather than grammar, and suggests that being 'mentioned' is a prerequisite for an entity to influence the local context. We adapted a modern neural model KVN by integrating the concept of mentioned status from CT, treating the frequency of a entity's occurrence as the primary indicator of its 'mentioned' status. Our proposed enhancement consistently improved the performance of various coreference tasks across multiple datasets, and provided valuable insights into the applicability of CT's principles in the contemporary era of artificial intelligence.

The spread of location services has been fueled by the need to estimate distances between two points, often informed by WiFi signals. However, the lack of comprehensive data regarding various methods of measuring WiFi ranges has hindered comprehensive research. In this study, multiple WiFi range estimation techniques are examined and compared, focusing on signal strength indicators such as RSSI, first arrival, and last arrival. By conducting experiments in similar environments with consistent devices and access points, it was found that the relationship between range and signal strength is approximately exponential for most methods, with a notable exception of the last arrival method, which displays a near-linear pattern. Furthermore, the implications of this discovery are highlighted, particularly in relation to estimating range from known data. Ultimately, the findings provide a valuable resource for researchers and development of more accurate positioning systems.

As beam energy decreases, the Beam Disruption Instability (BDI) is exacerbated in LHC energy recovery linacs, with particularly severe outcomes for high-temperature filling schemes. This research investigates the impact of beam configuration on BDI effects, focusing on an EB1 configuration with only one filled arm of the accelerator. Comparative simulations and analytical calculations are performed on multi-arm filled scenarios to establish the extent of damage to beam pipe surfaces. Findings reveal that a single filled arm can result in up to 50 times more damage than a scenario with symmetrical filling, although this figure drops to around ten times with dual adjacent filling scenarios. To mitigate the impact of BDI, suggestions for modification of beam configuration are proposed, along with strategies for compensation through scrubbing or coating of the beam pipe.

Using $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory's extensive helicity symmetry, we have developed an updated set of parton-level cross-sections, specifically for two colorless bosons produced in a central emission process within the high-energy limit. Our work encompasses precise calculations of one-loop corrections and involves six distinct components made up of gluons, gluinos, and scalars. We have obtained the corresponding results for NNLO corrections to Higgs production via vector boson fusion at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), providing essential data for inelastic corrections to the standard model calculation. These calculations can also be utilized to determine the vector meson total cross-sections in hadron collisions. Furthermore, we have compiled previous results and part of the relevant literature into an accessible format. To facilitate this, we have compiled our results into a readily available format on the arXiv.

This code enables the visualization of M. Krivine's 1965 demonstration that in zero-temperature planar self-avoiding bristles with a non-zero monomer projection, there are regions inaccessible to the leading polymer segment, regardless of its position or orientation, relative to the brille's coordinate system. Additionally, it illustrates M. Laue's (2017) non-analytic finding on highly stretched, random brilles in melt conditions, showing that inaccessible regions can be virtually unattainable in certain directions, but significantly smaller than the excluded area created by a single monomer at moderate to high polymer densities.

A subset of vertices in a graph G is considered resolvable through an injective function $h$ that maps from the graph's edges and a specific power of its edges' Cartesian product to the vertices, when combined with a varying distance metric on the underlying structure. The smallest such subset is defined as the metric dimension of the graph. We are extending this concept to a variant called the $\frac13$-resolving set, using a reduced distance metric for non-negative distances between points. The distance is calculated based on the difference between the actual distance and the sum of two compensating functions representing lower and upper bounds. The minimum cardinality of a $\frac13$-resolving set is termed the reduced metric dimension. We are also considering the variation of this concept that incorporates the actual distance in the overall calculation, resulting in a variant called the short metric dimension. The paper provides an overview and fundamental properties of these concepts, and establishes relationships and comparisions between them and the original metric dimension. Additionally, we provide examples and proof illustrations to support the theoretical framework, including a method to compute the short metric dimension via a linear programming approach and the study of the relationship between the reduced and original metric dimensions.

A paper is presented that outlines a method for processing and analyzing Fermi-LAT all-sky images over a specific time period. Unlike previous studies, this research utilizes a machine learning classification algorithm to identify variable sources. By comparing various machine learning models, the Random Forest classifier demonstrated the best performance in detecting variable sources with an accuracy of 97%. This classifying engine is then applied to a 12-year observation period from 2008 - 2019. A new catalog comprising 64 source directions is created after filtering out areas of high variability caused by the lunar reflection and known highly variable areas. These locations may represent regions of low sensitivity, reflection, or may be related to variable astronomical objects. The provided code is accessible at https://github.com/andrewjs/fermi-ll.

A serial dictatorship mechanism is a method of reaching an efficient agreement among self-sufficient agents who take turns offering trade proposals to others, which, if accepted, are considered final and irrevocable. Given a setting where agents offer proposals to potentially different groups, and considering the limitations of available research on potential improvements, my proposed enhanced method, called the private serial dictatorship mechanism, maintains the same level of potential gain as the original serial dictatorship method, and, in some cases, offers the same level of potential benefit, while also expanding the range where it can match the original method. To achieve this, the proposed mechanism requires very little to no information, such as possible payoffs that may be lost.

We developed a method to identify binary asteroids by analyzing historical five-color photometric data from the Pan-STARRS1 archive, utilizing a new metric based on light curve variation and range. This approach allowed us to detect 17 asteroids with significant orbital perturbations, which were noted with question marks due to the single-pass limitation of our technique. A separate analysis of objects exhibiting short-period photometric variations was also conducted.

This study develops inference methods for nonlinear models in networks, which contain finite values and lack unit selection, by expanding the estimator with a spectral decomposition of the adjacency matrix. We apply this expansion to identify and assess partial linear regression models in networks, and also examine how network peer effects can be misleading. Through simulation, we discover that expanding the threshold for an estimated peer influence parameter yields more reliable confidence intervals, and statistical information reveals that high-threshold networks provide clearer peer influence, while highly connected networks offer little new insight.
This paper establishes a novel version of the Leibniz Rule for the Riemann-Liouville variable-order fractional integral and derivative. A proof for the theorem's validity is provided in the article.

This paper is a unique resource for-reinforcement learning practitioners, as it explores how to develop a Theory-of-Mind (TOM) agent leading a Dungeons and Dragons game.
Our main contributions include methods for an DM to lead the game by learning from human demonstrations and from the players, and for the players to effectively engage with the DM when using a TOM agent.
To put these methods into practice, we created a simulator that replicates a D&D game session, and we evaluated learning to lead with a TOM and engaging with such an agent.
The results show that a TOM-based leader can effectively guide the game, as well as how players respond when they actively feedback to the learning agent.

The intricate folding and knotting of proteins serve as a subject of research in theoretical biology and topology. While the topological aspects of protein knots have been extensively researched, the complex dynamics and kinetics of knot formation and un-knotting remain challenging to understand. A novel approach is proposed in this study, combining statistical topology and Dijkstra's algorithm to identify the most probable transitions and reversals of protein configurations, bypassing the limitations of molecular dynamics simulations. This method is applied to the tyrosine-triptych knotted protein (Pyx), utilizing an exhaustive list of its possible configurations. The resulting bending pathways are visualized geometrically and geometrically-reduced forms are mapped onto the 3_1 knot space, revealing that Pyx primarily bends around its central core, with side chains flexing more than the backbone. The findings of this study provide a foundation for experimental and theoretical investigations into the mechanisms underlying protein knot formation.

We establish that for any positive integer $n \geq 1$, the symplectic mapping group of the blowup of $\mathbb{T}^{2n}$ at the origin of its coordinate space is not residually finite. Moreover, given two functions $\textsc{grow}_1$ and $\textsc{grow}_2$ on $n$, there exist disjoint sets of integers $I_1(n, \textsc{grow}_1)$ and $I_2(n, \textsc{grow}_2)$, both containing all sufficiently large $n$, with the following properties: for any $n$ in $I_1(n, \textsc{grow}_1)$, the abelianization of finitely generated nilpotent subgroups of the symplectic virtual tower of groups $\til{T}^{2n}\bigg{(}\text{Bl}_0(\text{Bl}_0(...\text{Bl}_0(\mathbb{T}^{2n})...)...)$ at the polar point ... at the polar point)$ exists but its growth is bounded by a function $\textsc{grow}_1(n)$. For any $n$ in $I_2(n, \textsc{grow}_2)$, the growth of the abelianization of these nilpotent subgroups is constrained by a function $\textsc{grow}_2(n)$.

A variation of the Nambu-Goldstone theorem will be presented, demonstrating how a non-zero vacuum expectation value of a local field operator can lead to an additional, unnecessary consequence. This consequence will be shown to equate to either the breaking of Lorentz invariance or causality violation. These principles will be applied to both standard and non-standard spontaneous symmetries. Furthermore, we will discuss how this phenomenon is related to the Stueckelberg mechanism, the inequivalence of vacuum states, and the possible emergence of massive or massless non-Abelian bosons. Notably, this phenomenon is distinct from the conventional type of spontaneous symmetry breaking, which only guarantees the existence of a massless scalar boson.

To enhance what large language models understand, researchers have been utilizing counterfactuals, which provide information that contrasts with what the models already know, building on the foundations established by text for knowledge. However, existing approaches in utilizing phrasal counterfactuals often leave models uncertain due to the use of indicators such as "actually" or "but", which reflect the original framework. In recent developments, utilizing indicator-free counterfactuals has gained popularity, as it implies more significant alterations to the models' understanding. Nevertheless, this method lacks consistency in applying counterfactuals uniformly. In response, a far more extensive set of phrasal counterfactuals has been created, drawing from six distinct types and ten verification methods, which targets large language models and applies to any in general. A automatic algorithm has been developed to produce over 300,000 valid counterfactuals that are verified by the models' own outputs, demonstrating that using such counterfactuals compels models' understanding to change significantly, as revealed by various assessments, including the fascinating result that models' sensitivity to indicators has been identified but also rejected. Finally, a mechanism for accurately selecting low-variance counterfactuals has been proposed, and the counterfactual framework has shown its utility by detecting bias and stoic properties in models' understanding. The counterfactuals produced are publicly accessible at the following link: https://github.com/AmitH99/DISCUS.

Enabling the creation of highly pure heusler compounds within graphene-bound sapphire structures requires an innovative method of growth. A new approach, combining remote, ion-pinhole, and van der Waals epitaxy, has been developed to facilitate this requirement. This method permits growth techniques similar to those used for traditional heusler compounds while providing the distinct advantages of van der Waals epitaxy. By utilizing this new technique, researchers were able to produce excellent quality films of GaP-based heusler material (CGOPH) on graphene/cubic sapphire within 480 minutes. Preliminary results indicate that this approach can also be applied to engineer various other non-symmetrical cubic heusler compounds.

Let $f$ be a prime number greater than or equal to 2. In this figure, we define a $\mathbb{Z}_f\mathbb{Z}_{f^2}$-linear code $C$ as the image of a homomorphism whose kernel has a specific dimension, which depends on the dimensions of its parts in $\mathbb{Z}_f^ {n}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{f^2}^{m}$. We develop a formula to calculate the dimension of such codes, which in turn allows us to investigate the properties of codes with minimum Hamming distance, particularly those that are considered quasi-optimal, whose characteristics are described in detail. Of particular interest are codes mapped from a homomorphism whose kernel has a dimension of $n$, and codes mapped from a homomorphism whose kernel has a dimension of $n-1$, both of which we fully characterize. As an example, we provide methods to construct $f$-potentially good $\mathbb{Z}_f\mathbb{Z}_{f^2}$-linear codes with the desired distance properties.

In supervised learning, models are typically trained to distinguish between multiple classes, but what happens when there's only one positive label for a particular instance? This single label could represent just one of several classes the instance belongs to, or it could be the sole class it fits. Treating this as a single-class problem limits the utility of valuable data and creates unnecessary costs by requiring confirmation of negative labels for other classes. We investigate this unexplored potential of multi-label data containing single positive labels, and propose a novel active learning strategy that adapts to both scenarios automatically. We also introduce a simpler alternative that achieves comparable performance. Our method's effectiveness is demonstrated through experiments on various datasets, showing significant improvements over using just the single label for classification.

This study examines the concept of Hilbert space in the context of Hilbert space mechanics using the lens of algebraic semantics. A key aspect explored is the 2-categorical adjunction between the 2-functor that constructs algebras and a 2-functor that defines observables and states. A key finding of the research is the conversion of a 2-categorical adjunction into a 2-categorical monad, which can then be used to define the Hilbert space algebra. The outcomes of the research are presented in the form of theorems, lemmas, and a coherent narrative.

We propose a novel theoretical model to explain the high-energy gamma-rays detected from energy-dispersed radio galaxies. In this model, a massive, high-speed gamma-ray gamma-ray disk is held in place by strong magnetic fields around the galaxy's core, and its gamma-rays are trapped and scattered by Compton effect due to the intense and varying magnetic field, contributing significantly to the observed data.

If a galaxy has a massive disk and strong magnetic fields, it could appear as a source of Type II radio energy and exhibit strong shifts in optical light, and if the fields or disk change, it could show shifts in optical light without appearing as a blazar. The model predicts that roughly 10% to 50% of the nearby energy-dispersed radio galaxies have gamma-ray energy, and approximately 50 to 500 GeV is the typical energy range where they lose gamma-rays due to the scattering of the Compton effect.

The model also suggests that supermassive galaxies with strong magnetic fields around their cores could produce distant gamma-rays by capturing gamma-ray-dispersed energy in the range of 10 keV to 100 TeV, and could significantly impact the observed data from the Fermi and HESS space telescopes.

A noisy environment during heart sound examination hinders accurate
diagnosis, as vibrations and pressures caused by surrounding sounds can
distort heart sound signals and hinder the detection of defects. To develop
diagnostic methods that work in real-world conditions, a method must be
created to distinguish between distorted and undistorted heart sound data. In this
study, an artificial intelligence-based approach is used to distinguish between
heart sound data recorded under noisy conditions and those recorded in quiet
conditions. A dataset of heart sounds was created to test and demonstrate the
effectiveness of a proposed heart sound classification model that accounts for
recorded sounds' additive and non-linear distortion under noisy environments.

The rapid expansion of computing power and the prevalence of cloud services have allowed for significant growth in mobile health applications, but this also raises major privacy concerns related to personal health data stored on wearables. To address these worries and capitalize on the benefits of advanced technology, transfer learning has the potential to play a key role. This role would require trustworthy data providers to collect large, diverse datasets from multiple wearables, and then train a model that can be transferred to new users. However, various limitations have been identified in existing frameworks, including issues with data security, wearable resource constraints, and information exposure. To overcome these challenges, we designed FedHealth, a first-ever federated transfer learning framework for wearable medical monitoring. FedHealth enables a secure collection of data, training on information split across many devices, and a model that is tailored to each user in a decentralized environment. During this environment, a protocol was established for the OCB+ encryption of local data, and a federated transfer learning algorithm developed on edge devices. As a result, an end-to-end encrypted model is obtained that is accurate and highly effective. Experimentation has verified FedHealth's success, demonstrating a precise blood glucose level prediction with an average root squared error of 10.01 split across eight datasets. The results highlight the advantages of FedHealth in ensuring data security and wearables' flexible data handling capabilities.

This note examines the underlying connections between various portfolio optimization
methods that have been proposed to address the limitations of Markowitz's mean-variance
technique in assessing and assessing asset performance over time. We establish a distinction
between cases where data is assumed to follow a fixed, known distribution and scenarios
where the distribution is treated as non-stationary and must be inferred from available
data. Within the framework of the former case, we identify when different methods, including
maximal expected utility, quasi-variance, portfolio tau-shrinkage, and leverage-based
portfolio approaches yield similar outcomes.

The world is becoming increasingly automated, with machines taking over simple tasks for us. While this trend is taking shape in various sectors like manufacturing and agriculture, its potential has yet to be fully realized in the tech industry. To bridge this gap, we introduce A2S2: a comprehensive framework for automating software-related processes. A2S2 encompasses a set of specialized tools that can be applied to a wide range of development issues, including making open-source projects usable for the general public, securing closed-source enterprise software, and translating mobile applications to new languages. Although Bots and Scripts have been around for some time, they are limited in their functionality compared to A2S2, which is designed to be modular and adaptable to different scenarios. A2S2 achieves this by breaking down complex tasks into smaller, more manageable components that can be easily swapped out or upgraded. We have demonstrated the versatility of A2S2 by using it for three distinct projects, but its modularity allows for even broader applications in the future.

Consider a variation of the optimal stopping problem where the candidate for the reward at the moment of completion of the task must exceed the cost of departure at a specific point in time. In our study, we re-examine a particular aspect of this problem, which we think is worth more attention than it has been regarded, namely, when the cost process includes infinite jumps. We provide an example to show that even in this scenario, a optimal stopping time can be found, thus contradicting the opposite claim made in a 2013 article by H. Pham, M. Jeanjean and F. Le Duze, who believed that the existence of such a solution is mutually exclusive to when the sample path of the cost process is right-continuous.

A significant level of interest is currently being poked at the light-neutrino generation mechanism, as the scope of the Standard Model gets expanded. A specific type of scalar type II leptoquark, denoted as $S_2$, which interacts with quarks and neutrinos, is being examined within a minimal framework. This examination reveals that the leptoquark $S_2$ must be treated in a non-universal manner across the three generations of quarks, in order to satisfy the observed data. A non-universal approach results in a distinct signature at the LHC, offering a testable prediction for this model. Furthermore, a connection is discovered between the leptoquark mass bounds and the neutrino oscillation parameters in this examination.

Researchers are increasingly utilizing the non-thermal radiative features of ionized carbon lines to gain insights into the physical characteristics of galaxies. To better understand this process, we examined the relationship between carbon monoxide and non-thermal carbon lines using a sample of starburst and main sequence galaxies. This analysis revealed that a substantial number of lines, particularly in local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE), exhibit non-thermal radiative excitation. As the radiative field strength rises, this excitation's impact diminishes. Furthermore, we developed a analysis framework based on radiative transfer and rate equations, which indicates that these non-thermal features provide valuable information about the radiative field strength and large width lines offer a more accurate assessment of velocity structures. This approach is supported by a rate equation study, which confirms our modeling and demonstrates that the non-thermal effects are more pronounced in galaxies with dense, narrow lines. These findings are also applicable to analysis of external galaxies and the radiative properties of molecular gas, including the potential use of carbon lines as a substitute for carbon monoxide lines in the far-infrared and submillimeter spectra of galaxies. This shift is especially beneficial for gaia-based analysis, which relies on grism spectra and provides an in-depth examination of velocity structures in molecular gas of galaxies using carbon monoxide and non-thermal carbon lines.

This paper builds on the 2019 work by Avila-Campbell and Hunter concerning hyperplane arrangements characterized by a specific minimum Hamming distance of $d$. The authors of the present paper are interested in the case where the minimum distance is $3$. Given an arrangement $\mathcal{H}$ of $n$ hyperplanes in a space $X$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, we define a unique arrangement $\mathcal{G}$ with a minimum distance of $3$, such that an increase in size from $\mathcal{G}$ to any larger arrangement $\mathcal{K}$ that contains $\mathcal{G}$ and has a minimum distance of $3$ requires the addition of at least $n$ hyperplanes. If the minimum distance of the arrangement $\mathcal{H}$ is at least $3$, we demonstrate that the arrangement $\mathcal{G}$ is a subset of $\mathcal{H}$. Moreover, an interesting property is found where the number of hyperplanes in the arrangement $\mathcal{H}$ is congruent to the number of hyperplanes in the arrangement $\mathcal{K}$, which can be expressed as $|\mathcal{H}| \equiv |\mathcal{K}| \pmod{n}$.

Researchers using Pulsar Timing Arrays are preparing to detect low-frequency gravitational waves, which may provide insights into supermassive binary sources. To accurately search for these signals, computationally intensive simulations in full general relativity are necessary. While simplified models have been used so far, the precision of these models may limit the sensitivity of the searches. In this study, we compare various post-Newtonian approximations of accurate general relativistic simulations to determine which offer similar precision but at a lower computational cost. By analyzing the differences between these models' representations of binary orbital evolution, we find that a specific approximations offers a similar level of precision to the most accurate benchmark at a significantly reduced computational expense. This preferred approximation is roughly two orders of magnitude faster than the most accurate model and about ten times faster than the next fastest model. Consequently, this model offers an ideal balance between precision and efficiency for simulations used in searches guided the Pulsar Timing Array.

We establish that in ASEP, the velocities of particles form a Markov process under the step initial condition, which converges to the GUE-PPW velocity process as $N$ approaches infinity. Additionally, we derive exact formulas for the expected value and variance of $x_1(t)$, showing that they scale as $O(\sqrt{t})$. These findings validate a conjecture made by van Moer for the case where $N=1$ and the particles are confined within $[0,1]$.

Comprehensive mathematical models have historically lacked real-world application until the current epidemic. These models are now being utilized to derive crucial insights and inform public health measures to mitigate transmission. We examine various model structures employed in connection with the ongoing outbreak and associated data, including ordinary and stochastic differential models, as well as spatial considerations. We discuss their limitations and potential for improvement in light of lessons from the present epidemic and past experiences. We consider novel approaches that integrate multiple model types and propose a unified conceptual framework for effective outbreak modelling. This framework includes critical assessment of model parameters, accounting for the impact of interventions on transmission, and accounting for spatial considerations. We argue that combining these elements into a singular framework for modelling across various geographical regions is an area for future research. We also propose incorporating network considerations into future models and utilize this framework to introduce the associated mathematics. We hope that this examination of model structures will encourage more rigorous public health modelling in future studies.

We studied how laser light affects spinor atoms-molecules reaction, specifically the 2+1 body recombination process. This influence is represented by an effective potential in the equation that describes the atom-molecule system. As the effective potential simulates a magnetic field, it results in an interesting spin precession between the two possible configurations of the atom-molecule system, analogous to the Mashke effect. This precession can be manipulated by adjusting the laser light's intensity. Furthermore, an expression was derived to describe the phase of spin precession, which depends on fundamental physical constants and the properties of the effective potential.

This study focuses on enhancing the efficiency of DNA storage protocols, specifically addressing two challenging aspects.  The creation of a hierarchical code structure is hampered by the necessity to verify the integrity of underlying error-correcting codes, a process that can be time-consuming due to the large scale of checks involved.  In addition, modifying stored data within a hierarchical framework requires complete DNA synthesis to maintain the code's efficiency, a practice which increases both cost and environmental impact.  To address these challenges, we propose a novel hierarchical code known as a Check-and-Replace code (CAR code).  The sub-codes in this system are easily verifiable, allowing the intended structure to be confirmed simply by reading the beginning segments of the DNA strands.  Furthermore, the code's efficient modified refresh cost enables data updates with a minimal requirement for new DNA synthesis.  To evaluate its real-world applicability, we conducted a case study using a library dataset comprising one million images, which required around 140 megabytes of DNA data.  In comparison to its hierarchical counterpart, a code derived from erasure correction, a CAR code offers a 38% to 55% improvement in refresh cost efficiency and provides a 5 orders of magnitude gain in verification speed.

Engineers working with hydrological models rely on numerical solvers for the shallow water equations, despite their simplicity, due to the equations' nonlinear nature and the intricate geometries of real-world terrains. This research proposes a profound geometrically flexible approach by combining a sophisticated coordinate system that adapts to complex terrains with the power of deep learning to accelerate solver development. When applied to a standard flat-geometry test case, our method achieves nearly a 200-fold reduction in solver time compared to conventional methods. If integrated with the SHAPING2 tool, our approach significantly expands our capability to model extremely complex geometries with over 10 million boundary elements, while maintaining the rapid speeds of our current 10k-element geometries.

Mobile photography benefits from high-dynamic-range (HDR) technology, which combines multiple exposures of the same scene to create an image with an expanded dynamic range. This research proposes a machine learning approach that automatically selects the optimal exposures for composing an HDR image on mobile devices. The method leverages historical camera data from a mobile device to select exposures, and makes room for human input by allowing users to adjust combination weights of specific exposures. A camcorder experiment demonstrates a 2dB improvement in signal-to-noise ratio compared to standard HDR techniques, without increasing exposure variance. This noise model is then used to develop an optimal blending method that accounts for differences in image noise levels. The resulting system is demonstrated through an Android mobile application.

As the application of neural networks in critical areas such as healthcare and legal systems intensifies, the need to explain their decisions becomes more apparent. Neural network "if-then" rules have emerged as potential explanations, yet existing methods for extraction often yield large numbers of complex rules. A potential solution is the Search for Causal Neural Networks (SCNN) algorithm, which generates a set of concise, human-understandable rules by dividing the data and training sub-networks. Each network learns to make correct predictions under specific conditions defined by the rules. We evaluated SCNN in ten scenarios, comparing it to standard neural network models and current explanation methods. We found that SCNN always produces a set of explanation rules that can replicate the performance of a single high-accuracy network. In five cases, it even matched or exceeded the accuracy of the best neural network. We believe this result signifies that SCNN has successfully identified the underlying cause-and-effect structure of the problems it was given.

This unconvincing b-principle explains why, according to the Pandharipande-Pirola inventory, nearly all bipartite plane partition variables in the expanded Chern-Simons partition function on the two-dimensional sphere with a negative one link defect, are coefficients that correspond to configurations involving six or more parts.

In this study, we investigate the scalability of multilevel preconditioners for cardiac mechanics using finite elements. Using a physiologically accurate model of a murine left ventricle, we employ a phase field method to formulate the problem and utilize an augmented Lagrangian approach to handle incompressibility. By applying an iterative solver based on a multigrid method for the nonlinear problem and investigating its parallel performance on up to 4096 processors, we examine the effectiveness of various multilevel approaches with different data partitions. Our results, obtained with 1 and 10 times physiological loadings, reveal the suitability of a specific multilevel method combined with an ILU(0) smoothing technique for highly parallel settings.

This study investigates the relationship between the spatial distribution of permeability in a 2D Hele-Shaw apparatus and the non-Gaussian diffusion of fluid particles. By employing the Boxcar, Log-Normal, and Power Law models to map spatial variations of permeability, researchers found that these scenarios correspond to non-Gaussian diffusion characterized by non-zero kurtosis and skewness. In contrast to previous studies, this study uses the probability density evolution equation (PEEE) to provide an analytical approach to tracking non-Gaussian diffusion. The PEEE method allows for the calculation of diffusion statistics - mean, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis - as functions of time. The predicted non-Gaussian statistics generated through the PEEE method show a strong correlation with the experimental measurements taken from tracer gas simulations.

A unifying mathematical framework is presented that encompasses the optical behavior of resonators and waveguides, covering both straight configurations and curved geometries. This framework accounts for both linear and Kerr nonlinear interactions. By applying this theory, we derive explicit formulas to describe the outcome of such interactions in detail. Our findings are presented across a range of scenarios with varying degrees of coupling strength. This includes situations where there is significant optical coupling, as well as weak coupling resulting in shifts of frequency. Findings from this study provide a rigorous basis for experimental observation of curved geometry-induced frequency shifts in this context.

To develop a high-fidelity turbulence model through machine learning, this study employs a generative adversarial network (GAN) to generate turbulent images from smooth flow patterns, overcoming the issue of low-resolution flow field data. A primary challenge in evaluating these generated images is addressing the lack of an objective theory for turbulence and the difficulty in measuring turbulent flow at high resolution, which hinders network performance assessment. To overcome this measurement challenge, the network is trained and assessed using TUEVAL, a high-speed, multi-reynolds number wind tunnel facility, which is equipped with high-resolution imaging capabilities. The network is trained to generate turbulent flow images from smooth flow patterns, and this process is evaluated across a 20-fold range of reynolds numbers. The resulting images are then compared to traditional skin friction measurements to verify their accuracy. The GAN successfully generates images that closely resemble the experimental measurements, however, it also introduces subtle discrepancies in skin friction distribution and failure regions, which shift with changing reynolds numbers. The network's performance is also assessed based on its reduced data dimensionality, which is a significant advantage given the high-resolution nature of images. The limitations in measuring the network's TUEVAL images are further explored, and this study is the first known instance of applying a learning-based image reconstruction technique in a wind tunnel, which has several potential applications beyond its current scope.

Strengthening autonomous vehicles and other sophisticated driving systems calls for continuous improvements, which is best achieved through advanced, lifelong reinforcement methods. However, these cutting-edge techniques are not well-tested due to the prevalence of supervision learning among current evaluations. To rectify this gap, we propose L2Explorer, a comprehensive and open-source driving simulation environment that supports a wide range of learning approaches, including reinforcement and supervised methods. By utilizing standardized vehicle dynamics and high-fidelity textures, L2Explorer enables realistic driving experiences. It features a versatile interface that is easily extensible, with its core components documented and its source code available on GitHub. To facilitate the adoption of lifelong learning techniques, we provide initial results and a dataset for comparison purposes. Furthermore, we present a multi-policy approach that attains superior performance in the devised task. We anticipate that L2Explorer will prove to be a valuable and versatile tool for future research and development in autonomous driving systems.

Human learning and understanding rely heavily on a balanced approach of receiving guidance through feedback and discovering new patterns independently. To incorporate this dual approach of supervision and exploration into a system capable of analyzing process models and data, a novel framework is developed, termed SupEx. In the SupEx method, a declared process is continuously updated as it processes a sequence of events, represented as a stream. This dynamic process produces system outputs, also in the form of streams, which are compared against expected outcomes, or specifications, to identify discrepancies or noise. To efficiently resolve these differences, a specialized exploration algorithm is employed, tailored to the characteristics of process models and sequences. The SupEx approach integrates three key process analysis techniques – supervision, exploration, and learning – and is demonstrated to be a cohesive and effective strategy. To illustrate the SupEx approach in a practical setting, a system is built that combines monitoring, exploration, and repair techniques for process models, and yields enhanced results compared to a technique that relies solely on exploration for exploring temporal sequences.

This paper provides an overview and analysis of various compactification methods for moduli spaces, with a focus on their relationship to the study of differential equations and F-gaugetheory. We examine several prominent compactification techniques, including Geometric Invariant Theory, boundary behavior, Hodge-theoretic approaches, boundary compactification, and Drinfeld's work. We discuss the pros and cons of each method and highlight open questions in this area of research.

We investigated 142 star-forming galaxies with masses between 10^9 and 10^11 solar masses and intermediate colors, many of which were from existing studies, using a model that considers bulge growth. We used the 2D projection restoration method to recover non-linear relationships that were lost during photometric measurements and restored the star formation sequences. By analyzing the galaxies, we created specific subgroups based on their super star clusters and bulge-to-disk ratios, then compared their specific star formation rates (sSFR) at high masses. We found that galaxies with massive super star clusters and those with prominent bulges tend to have lower sSFRs due to different physical mechanisms. We also found that color alone can't accurately predict the frequency of massive star clusters in galaxies, and our findings offer an updated framework for understanding the main sequence of galaxies, including the break known as the M* sequence.

This paper proposes a novel approach to sentiment assessment across different languages by leveraging an efficient, neural-based method. Our model uses a unified neural structure with task-specific sentiment classifiers for source languages and a universal classifier for the target language. By sharing representation spaces and splitting training data, this approach achieves improved performance. To demonstrate, we developed a cross-lingual sentiment model that excels at transferring knowledge from English to non-English languages. Our results show that our model outperforms existing methods in nine non-English languages on both intrinsic and extrinsic evaluations. Additionally, we release our comprehensive corpus of multilingual labeled texts to facilitate future research.

This paper investigates data patterns from X-ray images of patients with COVID-19, focusing on patients requiring intensive care.
An exploration of the relationship between requiring ICU treatment and the severity of illness is conducted, considering various factors 
such as age, gender, and symptoms. Additionally, the suitability of existing datasets for training image classification models is assessed.

We demonstrate that the simplicial looping operation preserves the property of being a simplicial group, with specific conditions under the functoriality of the simplicial delooping. Additionally, we identify the precise circumstances under which the nth simplicial delooping of a simplicial looped space forms a simplicial group.

This paper investigates the issue of false positives in visual relationship detection, a significant challenge that has hindered the practical application of this technology. Our analysis reveals that the current primary relationship detection methods fail to effectively identify false positives due to three main causes: ambiguous object relationships, relationships between identical objects, and relationships between different object instances. To address this problem, we propose a novel framework for visual relationship detection that incorporates a multi-stage detection process. In our stage-one approach, we identify potential relationships between object pairs and filter out ambiguous relationships. Our stage-two method then seeks to resolve the issue of relationships between identical objects by proposing a same-instance relationship detection framework. Our proposed two-stage method yields significant performance gains over the current state-of-the-art, particularly in terms of minimizing false positives. Our data showcases the effectiveness of this approach in improving detection accuracy.

We've analyzed the galaxy GC44 at a rate of 3 per square centimeter within the Coma cluster using deep HST imaging, revealing a prominent bulge, several distinct stellar streams, and an intrinsic ellipticity of 0.3. By estimating the bulge-to-total light ratio (B/T) at approximately 0.2 and an absolute magnitude of -2.4, we infer a total mass of roughly 3.8 * 10^8 solar masses for this galaxy. Evidence from color analysis suggests an lack of significant recent star formation in this region. Given the estimated intrinsic ellipticity and observed morphological asymmetry, we believe that interactions with neighboring galaxies have played a pivotal role in the structural evolution of GC44. A quantitative model of bulge growth, incorporating past accretion and mergers, suggests a particular scenario where a past head-on interaction with a dense galaxy cluster could have suppressed any further star formation, thus explaining the current status of GC44. Furthermore, we propose that a more recent oblique interaction with this galaxy cluster may have significantly influenced its internal structure, thus accounting for an observed mass distribution that differs from standard models.

On November 7, 2004, four space observatories discovered six major solar flares at 05:46 UT, 05:57 UT, and 06:12 UT of that morning, all classified as X-class. Although these flares were initially thought to be isolated events, further research revealed they were actually part of a single, large solar eruption, with evidence of it extending beyond X-class into extreme UV and radio spectra. Given their location in the sun's active region 10418, located near the equator, these solar flares had a substantial impact on the Earth's magnetosphere.

The process of a planet acquiring angular momentum through interactions with a protoplanetary disk is primarily governed by its shape, as rotational forces significantly impact the momentum transfer between the planet and the disk. This paper aims to analyze the angular momentum transfer in detail for different types of planets, taking into consideration various factors such as rotation rate, mass, and the properties of the surrounding gas. By employing a 3D simulation using the PLUTO code and the Herbig and Moiseiwitsch reflection model, we found that in most cases, only about 10% of outer trap bar gaps receive reflection, which has minimal impact on the specific momentum transfer. However, we discovered that planets can become locked to the local orbit of the disk, resulting in A-type star consumption. This effect is more pronounced in deeper reflection conditions and leads to significant consequences for the evolution of these stars.

Converging trends in artificial intelligence-generated content and the surge in fake news on social media have highlighted the critical issue of emergent false information. Unlike traditional news misinformation, emergent false news lacks prior indicators such as repetition or logical inconsistencies, posing a more subtle and deceptively normal threat to public safety. In this project, we introduce a novel emergent false news detection framework named FACILITATE, which leverages text and video content for comprehensive analysis. The FACILITATE framework comprises two main components: a data-enhancement module that utilizes an content-generator to create augmented clips based on text content, and an emergent false news classifier built upon a meta neural process network to accurately identify deceptive videos. To effectively handle the scarcity of labeled data, our solution integrates multiple learning strategies, including the contrastive and tri-triplet losses, to accurately rank videos as either emerggent misinformation or non-emergent misinformation. The efficacy of the FACILITATE framework is validated through comprehensive experiments, demonstrating superior results in emergent false news identification.

This research paper focuses on a convection equation defined on a two-dimensional periodic domain, which has been modified to include a periodic boundary condition. The study aims to identify solutions that satisfy the given boundary conditions while also preserving the mass conservation and total energy of the system. To achieve this objective, we have reformulated the original equation to incorporate the necessary boundary conditions, which in turn led to an investigation into the solvability of the resulting modified problem. The resulting anomalies have been described in detail in the context of this problem.

Recently, Golay complementary sets (GCS) were expanded upon from pairs to pairs of sequences, and a method to generate single-phase GCS from quadratic phase sequences was discovered by Colbourn and others. Furthermore, Colbourn and others demonstrated that GCS with a quadratic phase can be utilized to create single-phase GCS. In this study, we present two methods for producing multiphase GCS directly, including a class of multiphase GCS constructed from a specific type of binary sequence that was not previously documented, and several examples of these constructions are provided.

Silicon's specific crystal structure results in distinct electron and hole effective masses and movement characteristics within specific planes called valleys. This characteristic is considered beneficial for quantum computing due valley interaction and transfer between valley and spin states can be harnessed at a very small scale. In this study, we use spin-resolved scanning tunneling microscopy to study the behavior of holes in silicon and observe the simultaneous influence of valley and spin on their movement. We identify the relevant time and space scales for studying spin dynamics and confirm that Majorana holes have relatively long relaxation times. By comparing with theoretical models, we confirm that the zero-point motion of electrons in the effective mass wells provides long lifetimes for the $-1$ holes. This study is the first to observe and account for valley and momentum coupling effects in holes while maintaining accuracy, and the findings may have significant implications for the development of quantum computing in silicon.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) are an essential tool for analyzing complex system dynamics, forecasting time-series data, and unraveling the intricacy of multifaceted systems. As a leading application of deep learning, GNN-based models are being extensively utilized in various domains of industry and scholarly research. This paper provides a comprehensive framework, dissecting the core components and underlying principles of GNN-based models, and offers a detailed exploration of their use in analyzing complex system dynamics and forecasting time-series data. By examining the structural, input-output, and knowledge-infused approaches, we break down the technical nuances of GNN-based models and discuss their applicability to a wide array of applications. Furthermore, we discuss the limitations and potential pitfalls associated with these models, and suggest a research agenda to address their rectification and advancement. To facilitate a faster growth in this field, we propose a standardized evaluation framework, designed to guide future studies in comparing and assessing the effectiveness of GNN-based models across a wide range of applications.

This note provides an overview of cataloguing the homotopy groups of spheres, with a specific focus on the recently established works of multiple researchers, including those of Taylor, Tunnell, and Krashen. Additionally, a catalog is presented to summarize these developments.

Generating medical images with specific pathologies is essential for developing and testing automatic diagnosis systems. The accuracy of these systems heavily depends on the diversity of conditions represented in the training data. Although current methods can add lesions to images, they lack diversity, which limits their usefulness in creating balanced datasets for research. This paper introduces a new, highly versatile framework called Progressive Adversarial Variational Auto-Encoder (PAVAE) to generate a wide array of diverse cerebral lesions. By using multiple generators in a step-by-step process, we can create images with distinct and separate brain conditions, thereby enabling the creation of specialized datasets for each pathology. We show that the PAVAE model can generate images that are indistinguishable from real images with the desired condition, while other methods fail to achieve this level of accuracy. Moreover, we show that researchers can use this model to create balanced datasets by combining multiple distinct pathologies. Overall, the PAVAE model provides a significant advancement in generating diverse medical images, which is crucial for advancing the accuracy of automatic diagnosis systems.

GP 2 is a graph-based language designed for efficient program analysis and verification, leveraging graph transformation rules to ease these tasks. However, efficiently compiling GP 2 programs, particularly large-scale graphs, poses a significant challenge due to the resource-intensive nature of matching transformation rules. To tackle this challenge, an optimized GP 2 compiler, called EG2, is presented, which utilizes edge expansion diagrams to suggest candidate matching locations, significantly reducing the computational cost. In comparison to a naive approach, this improvement amounts to at least a 10-fold enhancement. Moreover, for real-world applications, EG2 exhibits an average speedup of 6.4 times with standard deviations accounted for.

Recently, sophisticated feature extraction methods based on deep learning have significantly improved the performance of various tasks including those implemented with traditional linear models. These advanced feature extraction techniques can be viewed through the lens of a unified framework, where components such as attention mechanisms, autoencoders, and generative adversarial networks are considered specialized representations. In this paper, we propose a consistent framework for research and development of novel unified feature extraction approaches. We also explore the applications of this framework in practical scenarios, employing it as an guide to develop a novel unified model for enhancing the performance of document representation using a multi-layered attention network, a reconstruction model based on graph variational attention autoencoder, and a competitive adversarial generator. Furthermore, we present empirical evidence from experiments conducted on two public datasets that demonstrate the superiority of our proposed unified model in comparison to several individual unified frameworks.

We have constructed a new collection of infinite simple groups based on twisted wreath structures, which can be classified as twisted wreath quotients of $C_p \rtimes S_n$ for a prime number $n$ within the range $n \le p < 4n - 4n^{.75}$. This collection is distinct from previously defined examples, including those of twisted wreath structure relative to $A_n$, $PSL_2(q)$, $PSL_3(q)$, and $ASU_3(q)$. Our findings contribute to a better understanding of the minimal normal subgroups of finite groups that prevent complete classification, specifically in relation to the Compton-Lnemberg conjecture.

Working with nominal (categorical) data that has many categories and a large number of groups is becoming increasingly common, but applying sparsity methods like the Group Lasso directly to these variables can lead to unnecessary data loss. To prevent unnecessary data loss while maintaining the sparsity methods' benefits, we propose a new way to encode nominal data that can be used with the Group Lasso method. Our proposed encoding retains some level of sparsity across each variable, rather than at the variable level. We show through theorems and computer simulations that this new encoding leads to better statistical performance. We also show through real-world application with the help of an R package, our method delivers superior results in terms of prediction accuracy.

Recent advances in large language models have achieved human-parity in various benchmarks for NLP tasks. However, these models struggle with handling structured knowledge, like tables and diagrams, which could significantly enhance their capabilities. To address this challenge, we developed ABILITY, a method that enables the stepwise translation of structured knowledge into natural language for Large Language Models. By breaking down the knowledge integration process into manageable steps, ABILITY guides the model to incorporate structured information seamlessly into the reasoning process. We validated our method through extensive experiments on various types of structured knowledge, including tables, graph knowledge, and mathematical formulas, showing substantial improvements in prediction accuracy when using the ABILITY framework.

This paper proposes a method to apply a practical spatial anti-aliasing technique to line junctions in vector maps for more accurate and aesthetically pleasing 3D representations. A lineside width field is utilized to signify the texture lines' effective width. An efficient algorithm is presented to compute this field, along with an optimization strategy to minimize storage requirements. By employing a simple sampling approach, the field can be quickly retrieved from a pre-rendered anti-aliasing texture. Comparative analysis shows that this method outperforms an existing mathematical model in terms of visual quality and efficiency, outdoing the MB function both computationally and qualitatively. Additionally, this paper explores various anti-aliasing application scenarios and provides an accessible understanding of the proposed technique.

To enhance the quality of speech on specific devices and applications, it is crucial to effectively reduce the noise in audio recordings, and this study introduces a new model called DPCRN for speech separation. Building upon the existing SPR network, DPCRN features a dual-path architecture that combines long short-term memory and vanilla recurrent networks, and employs two distinct sets of dilated convolution modules to capture both short-range and long-range spectral patterns. The set of model parameters for DPCRN is significantly smaller than that of the SPR network, and this study compares the two models across multiple datasets, showing that DPCRN outperforms the SPR network and other comparable models, and achieves a 65% reduction in the number of model parameters when compared to the SPR network.

Using multi-fluid modeling can provide a more comprehensive understanding of atmospheric convection by modeling individual cloud particles. To achieve such multi-fluid models, a crucial prerequisite is the development of reliable single-fluid convection models. In this work, we undertake a similar approach and initiate the creation of a novel multi-fluid model for Rayleigh-Benard convection. In this proposed framework, multiple horizontal layers of fluid participate in convection. Our plan to achieve this involves applying a similar transformation to the atmospheric convection model, known as the Large-Scale Model (LSM). To this end, we developed a single-column simulation (SCS) of 2D RBE convection for 8 versions with varying Sushman numbers. For comparison, existing multi-fluid and single-fluid models were also examined in this study. Notably, the proposed single-column simulation accurately replicates the characteristics of the most common single-fluid model. However, it failed to do so for the least common model. To address this challenge, the proposed simulation was modified by changing the manner in which heating and cooling occur at the boundaries. Moreover, the results obtained from this study are primarily limited to Sushman number effects. In the future, further studies will be conducted to also examine Prandtl number and scale effects.

In the vicinity of quantum resonators' transition frequencies where the Jaynes-Cummings effect occurs, pairs of uncoupled atoms can become genuinely entangled. Our research demonstrates that genuine multi-particle entanglement can arise from two-qubit Jaynes-Cummings interactions, specifically showing that three-qubit states with populations in only two levels of possible configurations can become genuinely multi-particle entangled through non-markovian dynamics. By accounting for the environment's impact on quantum systems, we provide an authentically entangled version of a recent finding. Furthermore, our study reveals conditions where multi-particle correlations surpass those described by the generalized Bell inequality. Utilating Rabi oscillations, we identify a method to verify genuine multi-particle entanglement without post-selection, utilizing only measurements from the ground state.

Our Twitter sentiment analysis method combines an ensemble approach with
LSTM-based classification of individual tweets. We first establish a
sentiment classification procedure for public figures on Facebook using
ensemble techniques, then apply this to the entire corpus of Twitter tweets. 
Instead of manually labeling each tweet as positive, negative, or neutral, we 
define inter-follower sentiment, then integrate this approach to create a new 
form of sentiment classification specific to Twitter users.

A theoretical framework based on shadow imaging can provide precise estimates of some key parameters in general relativity. In this paper, a method is developed to calculate the charge to mass ratio of an AdS black hole with varying degrees of non-linearity, which is derived from the Einstein-Maxwell-$\phi^2$ theory. By utilizing the preserved principles of shelf and horizon adiabatic invariance, this ratio can be determined within this specific non-abelian model. This research yields results that closely mirror those from previous studies based on applied physics principles, while also revealing a unique, new behavior. Furthermore, a connection is discovered and examined between the horizon area in this model and a phase transition of the corresponding isobaric shadow thermodynamics.

Recent advances in the expressions of changes in quantum states have been reflected in the Weyl and Q functions of phase space. These functions serve as tools for measuring the quantum entanglement and can be used to detect the onset of system-variable correlation. We have obtained corresponding operators that correspond to the S-matrix and quantum density matrix in terms of the Weyl symbol $\chi$ and quasi-probability function $Q$. These new symbols are derived from the Smith transform of the Fock space basis and can be calculated directly from the square root and product of two experimentally measurable signals. This makes them ideal for use in various applications, including our 3D-beam experiment, where we found that the S-matrix revealed beam entanglement beyond the Rayleigh range and captured the beam's axial shift that preceded the onset of transverse correlation.

With the rise of video streaming platforms, users can navigate through360-degree virtual travel videos, personalizing their viewing experience by
focusing on specific areas. However, this navigation may lead to missing
notable events that are outside their current view. This research develops a
model to anticipate the user's future viewing area, enabling content creators
to prioritize and make crucial content more visible, even from afar. We
process captions to extract semantic information, which is combined with
explicit details to train a predictor of future viewing areas. It evaluates
three different content importances within the scene and presents data from
real-world video meetings, along with annotations of future viewing areas. To
address this prediction challenge, we extend an existing approach and
